summary:
## First Quarter GDP Strength

Korea's economy is performing at the top of the OECD pack. Vice Finance Minister Heo Jang announced during an investor briefing in Paris that the nation achieved first-quarter GDP growth of 1.7% quarter-over-quarter, representing the strongest performance among OECD member countries to date. This remarkable achievement reflects the underlying strength of Korea's export-driven economy and represents a significant validation of the government's economic policies on the global stage.

## Export Boom Continues

The semiconductor super cycle is driving exceptional export performance. From January through May this year, Korea's exports surged 40% year-over-year, reaching approximately 390 billion dollars. This extraordinary growth trajectory underscores the critical importance of semiconductors and advanced technology products to Korea's economic expansion. The export momentum has become the primary engine pulling the overall economy forward, offsetting concerns in other sectors and justifying optimistic forecasts from international institutions.

## Current Account Surplus Record

Korea has now posted 36 consecutive months of current account surplus, with cumulative surpluses from January through April alone reaching an impressive 102.67 billion dollars, the largest on record. This extraordinary external balance reflects Korea's competitive positioning in global markets and robust demand for its products. The surplus demonstrates that the nation's export competitiveness remains formidable despite various global economic headwinds and geopolitical uncertainties.

## OECD Upgrades Forecast

The OECD significantly raised its Korea growth forecast, boosting the projection from 1.7% to 2.6% for the full year. Simultaneously, the organization lowered Korea's general government debt-to-GDP ratio outlook from 52.0% to 48.2% for this year, and from 55.0% to 50.2% for next year. These substantial upward revisions demonstrate growing international confidence in Korea's economic trajectory and fiscal sustainability, positioning the nation favorably compared to other advanced economies facing inflationary pressures and structural challenges.

## Currency Weakness Puzzle

Despite three decades of current account surpluses, the Korean won has weakened to its lowest level since the 2009 global financial crisis. The won-dollar exchange rate reached 1,539.10 won on today's trading, up 9.4 won from the previous close, with intraday highs threatening the 1,550 won level. This paradoxical weakness amid strong economic fundamentals reflects foreign investor outflows from domestic equities and broader global risk sentiment shifts driven by Middle East tensions and energy price volatility.

## Stock Market Turbulence

Korea's financial markets experienced what many are calling a Black Friday. The KOSPI index plummeted 478.82 points, or 5.54%, closing at 8,160.59, while the KOSDAQ fell 47.29 points, or 4.50%, to 1,002.44. Foreign investors have now sold Korean stocks for 20 consecutive trading days, triggering automatic circuit breakers that temporarily halted program selling. The sharp decline appears disconnected from Korea's strong economic fundamentals, instead reflecting global technology sector weakness and broader portfolio rebalancing by foreign institutional investors.

## Data Center Investment Acceleration

The government is fast-tracking a major artificial intelligence infrastructure project in Jangseong County, South Jeolla Province. A 400-billion-won advanced data center complex, part of the seventh Regional Activation Investment Fund project, will receive exemption from local fiscal investment reviews, enabling faster construction. The facility is targeted for completion by 2027 and operational launch by 2028, positioning South Korea as a key AI infrastructure hub in Asia. Deputy Prime Minister Gu Yun-chul emphasized that this investment strengthens regional AI infrastructure while supporting long-term economic growth.

## Capital Market Reform Narrative

Vice Minister Heo highlighted Korea's shift from Korea Discount to Korea Premium. The government emphasized corporate governance reforms, enhanced shareholder returns, and Commercial Code amendments designed to boost investor confidence. Since Korea's inclusion in the World Government Bond Index, foreign investors have injected 18.7 billion dollars net into domestic government bonds. These structural improvements address long-standing concerns about Korea's valuation discount and represent attempts to attract sustained foreign capital inflows.

## Real Estate Market Pressures

Seoul faces critical housing challenges as jeonse deposits plummet and monthly rents soar. Jeonse inventory declined 28.7% year-over-year and 20.7% since year-end 2025, dropping to just 18,455 listings. This shortage is pushing renters toward officetel properties, with officetel lease transactions rising 9.1% year-over-year in Seoul during the first four months of 2026. Mayor-elect Oh Se-hoon has identified real estate as Seoul's primary policy challenge, pledging to accelerate 310,000 housing units through private redevelopment and reconstruction projects by 2031 to stabilize prices through supply expansion.

## AI Profit Sharing Discussion

Employment Minister Kim Young-hun characterized the distribution of artificial intelligence excess profits as reinvestment and coexistence, not communism. He proposed adjusting contract prices with suppliers as one mechanism for sharing AI windfall gains, emphasizing that Samsung's remarkable performance results from dedicated labor-management cooperation. This signals the government's intent to establish new distribution rules through social dialogue, balancing corporate growth with broader economic equity concerns as AI reshapes competitive advantages.

## Global Uncertainties Persist

The Federal Reserve faces mounting inflation pressures, with the Beige Book confirming renewed energy-driven price pressures even as employment appears stable. Markets anticipate the Fed will hold rates steady at the June 16-17 FOMC meeting, though CME FedWatch data shows December rate increase probability has jumped to 41.1% from just 9.1% a month earlier, reflecting dramatically shifted market expectations regarding future monetary policy tightening.

## Investment Implications

For investors, Korea presents a paradoxical situation: exceptional economic fundamentals and export growth merit optimism, yet significant headwinds require caution. The won's weakness against the dollar may eventually support exporter earnings but creates currency risk for international portfolios. The KOSPI's sharp decline appears overdone relative to earnings quality, potentially offering entry points for patient capital. Watch the won-dollar rate closely at 1,550 won as a psychological and technical resistance level, with implications for foreign investor sentiment. The data center investment and AI infrastructure development signal long-term growth opportunities, but near-term volatility should be expected as foreign funds continue repositioning. General viewers should note that real estate pressures may moderate housing aspirations, yet supply-focused solutions under the new Seoul administration could eventually support market stabilization.
headline: Korea Posts OECD-Leading Growth Amid Won Weakness Concerns
